applies_why: The judge uses the cited verse(s)' not stating that Joseph begat the child as part of the basis for holding the defense.
quote: neither text states that Joseph begat the child ([L4]). Because the defender answered the witnesses pressed against the chain and neither withdrew nor suffered refutation of the declared links, the defense holds ([L4]).
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.
room: 'single verse does not state a link or its contrary': reading 1, the rule bars relying on any cited verse's silence about the link/contrary, even when phrased as 'neither text'; reading 2, it bars only an isolated single verse's silence, so a 'neither text' observation about two verses would fall outside it.
why: The judge's statement that the text(s) do not state the begetting and its HELD outcome make the non-statement a ground for STANDS, which K-S2 forbids.
